  45 │             (?:(?P<epoch>[0-9]+):)?               # epoch
  46 │             (?P<release>[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)*)      # release segment
  47 │             (?P<pre>                              # pre release

  50 │                 (?P<pre_n>[0-9]+)?                #  - pre-release number

 112 │             parts.append("{0}:".format(self._version.epoch))
 113 │

 115 │         parts.append(".".join(str(x) for x in self._version.release))

 117 │         # Pre-release

 179 │ def _parse_letter_version(letter, number):
 180 │     if letter:
 181 │         # We consider there to be an implicit 0 in a pre-release if there is
 182 │         # not a numeral associated with it.
 183 │         if number is None:
 184 │             number = 0
 185 │ 
 186 │         # We normalize any letters to their lower case form
 187 │         letter = letter.lower()
 188 │ 
 189 │         # We consider some words to be alternate spellings of other words and
 190 │         # in those cases we want to normalize the spellings to our preferred
 191 │         # spelling.
 192 │         if letter == "alpha":
 193 │             letter = "a"
 194 │         elif letter == "beta":
 195 │             letter = "b"
 196 │         elif letter == "rc":
 197 │             letter = "c"
 198 │ 
 199 │         return letter, int(number)

 202 │ def _parse_local_version(local):
 203 │     """
 204 │     Takes a string like abc.1.twelve and turns it into ("abc", 1, "twelve").
 205 │     """
 206 │     if local is not None:
 207 │         return tuple(
 208 │             part.lower() if not part.isdigit() else int(part)
 209 │             for part in local.split(".")
 210 │         )

 213 │ def _cmpkey(epoch, release, pre, post, dev, local):
 214 │     # When we compare a release version, we want to compare it with all of the
 215 │     # trailing zeros removed. So we'll use a reverse the list, drop all the now
 216 │     # leading zeros until we come to something non zero, then take the rest
 217 │     # re-reverse it back into the correct order and make it a tuple and use
 218 │     # that for our sorting key.
 219 │     release = tuple(
 220 │         reversed(list(
 221 │             itertools.dropwhile(
 222 │                 lambda x: x == 0,
 223 │                 reversed(release),
 224 │             )
 225 │         ))
 226 │     )
 227 │ 
 228 │     # We need to "trick" the sorting algorithm to put 1.0.dev0 before 1.0a0.
 229 │     # We'll do this by abusing the pre segment, but we _only_ want to do this
 230 │     # if there is not a pre or a post segment. If we have one of those then
 231 │     # the normal sorting rules will handle this case correctly.
 232 │     if pre is None and post is None and dev is not None:
 233 │         pre = -Infinity
 234 │     # Versions without a pre-release (except as noted above) should sort after
 235 │     # those with one.
 236 │     elif pre is None:
 237 │         pre = Infinity
 238 │ 
 239 │     # Versions without a post segment should sort before those with one.
 240 │     if post is None:
 241 │         post = -Infinity
 242 │ 
 243 │     # Versions without a development segment should sort after those with one.
 244 │     if dev is None:
 245 │         dev = Infinity
 246 │ 
 247 │     if local is None:
 248 │         # Versions without a local segment should sort before those with one.
 249 │         local = -Infinity
 250 │     else:
 251 │         # Versions with a local segment need that segment parsed to implement
 252 │         # the sorting rules in PEP440.
 253 │         # - Alpha numeric segments sort before numeric segments
 254 │         # - Alpha numeric segments sort lexicographically
 255 │         # - Numeric segments sort numerically
 256 │         # - Shorter versions sort before longer versions when the prefixes
 257 │         #   match exactly
 258 │         local = tuple(
 259 │             (i, "") if isinstance(i, int) else (-Infinity, i)
 260 │             for i in local
 261 │         )
 262 │ 
 263 │     return epoch, release, pre, post, dev, local

 272 │ class Specifier(object):

 274 │     _regex = re.compile(
 275 │         r"""

 277 │         (?P<operator>(~=|==|!=|<=|>=|<|>|===))

 279 │             (?:

 283 │                 # any semantic meaning from it. This operator is discouraged
 284 │                 # but included entirely as an escape hatch.
 285 │                 (?<====)  # Only match for the identity operator
 286 │                 .*        # We just match everything, since we are only testing
 287 │                           # for strict identity.
 288 │             )
 289 │             |
 290 │             (?:
 291 │                 # The (non)equality operators allow for wild card and local
 292 │                 # versions to be specified so we have to define these two
 293 │                 # operators separately to enable that.
 294 │                 (?<===|!=)            # Only match for equals and not equals
 295 │ 
 296 │                 (?:[0-9]+:)?          # epoch
 297 │                 [0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)*   # release
 298 │                 (?:[-\.]?(a|b|c|rc|alpha|beta)[0-9]*)? # pre release
 299 │                 (?:[-\.]?post[0-9]*)? # post release
 300 │ 
 301 │                 # You cannot use a wild card and a dev or local version
 302 │                 # together so group them with a | and make them optional.
 303 │                 (?:
 304 │                     (?:[-\.]?dev[0-9]*)?                       # dev release
 305 │                     (?:\+[a-z0-9]+(?:[a-z0-9_\.+]*[a-z0-9])?)? # local
 306 │                     |
 307 │                     \.\*  # Wild card syntax of .*
 308 │                 )?
 309 │             )
 310 │             |
 311 │             (?:
 312 │                 # The compatible operator requires at least two digits in the
 313 │                 # release segment.
 314 │                 (?<=~=)               # Only match for the compatible operator
 315 │ 
 316 │                 (?:[0-9]+:)?          # epoch
 317 │                 [0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)+   # release  (We have a + instead of a *)
 318 │                 (?:[-\.]?(a|b|c|rc|alpha|beta)[0-9]*)? # pre release
 319 │                 (?:[-\.]?post[0-9]*)? # post release
 320 │                 (?:[-\.]?dev[0-9]*)?  # dev release
 321 │             )
 322 │             |
 323 │             (?:
 324 │                 # All other operators only allow a sub set of what the
 325 │                 # (non)equality operators do. Specifically they do not allow
 326 │                 # local versions to be specified nor do they allow the prefix
 327 │                 # matching wild cards.
 328 │                 (?<!==|!=|~=)         # We have special cases for these
 329 │                                       # operators so we want to make sure they
 330 │                                       # don't match here.
 331 │ 
 332 │                 (?:[0-9]+:)?          # epoch
 333 │                 [0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)*   # release
 334 │                 (?:[-\.]?(a|b|c|rc|alpha|beta)[0-9]*)? # pre release
 335 │                 (?:[-\.]?post[0-9]*)? # post release
 336 │                 (?:[-\.]?dev[0-9]*)?  # dev release
 337 │             )
 338 │         )
 339 │         $
 340 │         """,
 341 │         re.VERBOSE | re.IGNORECASE,
 342 │     )
 343 │ 
 344 │     _operators = {
 345 │         "~=": "compatible",
 346 │         "==": "equal",
 347 │         "!=": "not_equal",
 348 │         "<=": "less_than_equal",
 349 │         ">=": "greater_than_equal",
 350 │         "<": "less_than",
 351 │         ">": "greater_than",
 352 │         "===": "identity",
 353 │     }
 354 │ 
 355 │     def __init__(self, specs, prereleases=False):
 356 │         # Normalize the specification to remove all of the whitespace
 357 │         specs = specs.replace(" ", "")
 358 │ 
 359 │         # Split on comma to get each individual specification
 360 │         _specs = set()
 361 │         for spec in specs.split(","):
 362 │             match = self._regex.search(spec)
 363 │             if not match:
 364 │                 raise InvalidSpecifier("Invalid specifier: '{0}'".format(spec))
 365 │ 
 366 │             _specs.add(
 367 │                 (match.group("operator"), match.group("version"))
 368 │             )
 369 │ 
 370 │         # Set a frozen set for our specifications
 371 │         self._specs = frozenset(_specs)
 372 │ 
 373 │     def __repr__(self):
 374 │         return "<Specifier({0})>".format(repr(str(self)))
 375 │ 
 376 │     def __str__(self):
 377 │         return ",".join(["".join(s) for s in sorted(self._specs)])
 378 │ 
 379 │     def __hash__(self):
 380 │         return hash(self._specs)
 381 │ 
 382 │     def __and__(self, other):
 383 │         if isinstance(other, string_types):
 384 │             other = Specifier(other)
 385 │         elif not isinstance(other, Specifier):
 386 │             return NotImplemented
 387 │ 
 388 │         return self.__class__(",".join([str(self), str(other)]))
 389 │ 
 390 │     def __eq__(self, other):
 391 │         if isinstance(other, string_types):
 392 │             other = Specifier(other)
 393 │         elif not isinstance(other, Specifier):
 394 │             return NotImplemented
 395 │ 
 396 │         return self._specs == other._specs
 397 │ 
 398 │     def __ne__(self, other):
 399 │         if isinstance(other, string_types):
 400 │             other = Specifier(other)
 401 │         elif not isinstance(other, Specifier):
 402 │             return NotImplemented
 403 │ 
 404 │         return self._specs != other._specs
 405 │ 
 406 │     def __contains__(self, item):
 407 │         # Normalize item to a Version, this allows us to have a shortcut for
 408 │         # ``"2.0" in Specifier(">=2")
 409 │         version_item = item
 410 │         if not isinstance(item, Version):
 411 │             try:
 412 │                 version_item = Version(item)
 413 │             except ValueError:
 414 │                 # If we cannot parse this as a version, then we can only
 415 │                 # support identity comparison so do a quick check to see if the
 416 │                 # spec contains any non identity specifiers
 417 │                 #
 418 │                 # This will return False if we do not have any specifiers, this
 419 │                 # is on purpose as a non PEP 440 version should require
 420 │                 # explicit opt in because otherwise they cannot be sanely
 421 │                 # prioritized
 422 │                 if (not self._specs
 423 │                         or any(op != "===" for op, _ in self._specs)):
 424 │                     return False
 425 │ 
 426 │         # Ensure that the passed in version matches all of our version
 427 │         # specifiers
 428 │         return all(
 429 │             self._get_operator(op)(
 430 │                 version_item if op != "===" else item,
 431 │                 spec,
 432 │             )
 433 │             for op, spec, in self._specs
 434 │         )
 435 │ 
 436 │     def _get_operator(self, op):
 437 │         return getattr(self, "_compare_{0}".format(self._operators[op]))
 438 │ 
 439 │     def _compare_compatible(self, prospective, spec):
 440 │         # Compatible releases have an equivalent combination of >= and ==. That
 441 │         # is that ~=2.2 is equivalent to >=2.2,==2.*. This allows us to
 442 │         # implement this in terms of the other specifiers instead of
 443 │         # implementing it ourselves. The only thing we need to do is construct
 444 │         # the other specifiers.
 445 │ 
 446 │         # We want everything but the last item in the version, but we want to
 447 │         # ignore post and dev releases and we want to treat the pre-release as
 448 │         # it's own separate segment.
 449 │         prefix = ".".join(
 450 │             list(
 451 │                 itertools.takewhile(
 452 │                     lambda x: (not x.startswith("post")
 453 │                                and not x.startswith("dev")),
 454 │                     _version_split(spec),
 455 │                 )
 456 │             )[:-1]
 457 │         )
 458 │ 
 459 │         # Add the prefix notation to the end of our string
 460 │         prefix += ".*"
 461 │ 
 462 │         return (self._get_operator(">=")(prospective, spec)
 463 │                 and self._get_operator("==")(prospective, prefix))
 464 │ 
 465 │     def _compare_equal(self, prospective, spec):
 466 │         # We need special logic to handle prefix matching
 467 │         if spec.endswith(".*"):
 468 │             # Split the spec out by dots, and pretend that there is an implicit
 469 │             # dot in between a release segment and a pre-release segment.
 470 │             spec = _version_split(spec[:-2])  # Remove the trailing .*
 471 │ 
 472 │             # Split the prospective version out by dots, and pretend that there
 473 │             # is an implicit dot in between a release segment and a pre-release
 474 │             # segment.
 475 │             prospective = _version_split(str(prospective))
 476 │ 
 477 │             # Shorten the prospective version to be the same length as the spec
 478 │             # so that we can determine if the specifier is a prefix of the
 479 │             # prospective version or not.
 480 │             prospective = prospective[:len(spec)]
 481 │ 
 482 │             # Pad out our two sides with zeros so that they both equal the same
 483 │             # length.
 484 │             spec, prospective = _pad_version(spec, prospective)
 485 │         else:
 486 │             # Convert our spec string into a Version
 487 │             spec = Version(spec)
 488 │ 
 489 │             # If the specifier does not have a local segment, then we want to
 490 │             # act as if the prospective version also does not have a local
 491 │             # segment.
 492 │             if not spec.local:
 493 │                 prospective = Version(prospective.public)
 494 │ 
 495 │         return prospective == spec
 496 │ 
 497 │     def _compare_not_equal(self, prospective, spec):
 498 │         return not self._compare_equal(prospective, spec)
 499 │ 
 500 │     def _compare_less_than_equal(self, prospective, spec):
 501 │         return prospective <= Version(spec)
 502 │ 
 503 │     def _compare_greater_than_equal(self, prospective, spec):
 504 │         return prospective >= Version(spec)
 505 │ 
 506 │     def _compare_less_than(self, prospective, spec):
 507 │         # Less than are defined as exclusive operators, this implies that
 508 │         # pre-releases do not match for the same series as the spec. This is
 509 │         # implemented by making <V imply !=V.*.
 510 │         return (prospective < Version(spec)
 511 │                 and self._get_operator("!=")(prospective, spec + ".*"))
 512 │ 
 513 │     def _compare_greater_than(self, prospective, spec):
 514 │         # Greater than are defined as exclusive operators, this implies that
 515 │         # pre-releases do not match for the same series as the spec. This is
 516 │         # implemented by making >V imply !=V.*.
 517 │         return (prospective > Version(spec)
 518 │                 and self._get_operator("!=")(prospective, spec + ".*"))
 519 │ 
 520 │     def _compare_identity(self, prospective, spec):
 521 │         return prospective.lower() == spec.lower()
 522 │ 
 523 │ 
 524 │ _prefix_regex = re.compile(r"^([0-9]+)((?:a|b|c|rc)[0-9]+)$")
 525 │ 
 526 │ 
 527 │ def _version_split(version):
 528 │     result = []
 529 │     for item in version.split("."):
 530 │         match = _prefix_regex.search(item)
 531 │         if match:
 532 │             result.extend(match.groups())
 533 │         else:
 534 │             result.append(item)
 535 │     return result
 536 │ 
 537 │ 
 538 │ def _pad_version(left, right):
 539 │     left_split, right_split = [], []
 540 │ 
 541 │     # Get the release segment of our versions
 542 │     left_split.append(list(itertools.takewhile(lambda x: x.isdigit(), left)))
 543 │     right_split.append(list(itertools.takewhile(lambda x: x.isdigit(), right)))
 544 │ 
 545 │     # Get the rest of our versions
 546 │     left_split.append(left[len(left_split):])
 547 │     right_split.append(left[len(right_split):])
 548 │ 
 549 │     # Insert our padding
 550 │     left_split.insert(
 551 │         1,
 552 │         ["0"] * max(0, len(right_split[0]) - len(left_split[0])),
 553 │     )
 554 │     right_split.insert(
 555 │         1,
 556 │         ["0"] * max(0, len(left_split[0]) - len(right_split[0])),
 557 │     )
 558 │ 
 559 │     return (
 560 │         list(itertools.chain(*left_split)),
 561 │         list(itertools.chain(*right_split)),
 562 │     )
